note: Every value here is invented. Field names and nesting follow the vendor documentation snapshot in ../api-snapshot.json and the shapes seen on the public demo agreement. This is a test of Quits-side extraction and reconciliation logic. It is NOT a migration of a real account and does not show that any real account returns data in this shape.

scenarios.name: unpaid
scenarios.description: One issued invoice with no payment. Residual equals gross. One attached document joined by accounting year and voucher number.

scenarios.name: fully_paid
scenarios.description: Invoice settled by one matching payment. Paid state is proven by the pair and the payment line, not a flag.

scenarios.name: partially_paid
scenarios.description: Invoice 1000.00 with a 400.00 payment matched. The pair shows full entry amounts; the applied 400.00 comes from amount minus remainder.

scenarios.name: credit_allocation
scenarios.description: Credit notes: fully offset, partially offset and still open. A credit note is a booked invoice with negative totals; only the pair links it to an invoice.

scenarios.name: unapplied_cash
scenarios.description: Payment larger than the invoice it was matched to, plus a payment on account matched to nothing. The surplus exists only as the payment's remainder.

scenarios.name: rounding
scenarios.description: Per-line VAT rounding and a non-zero roundingAmount whose relation to gross the vendor does not document. The validator accepts gross = net + VAT or net + VAT + rounding, and says so.

scenarios.name: foreign_currency
scenarios.description: EUR customer. Invoice fully paid at a different rate (exchange difference visible only in base amounts) and a partial EUR payment. exchangeRate is base units per 100 EUR.

scenarios.name: missing_documents
scenarios.description: Original PDF missing, PDF fetch failing, PDF never fetched, and a voucher dated outside the extracted accounting years.

scenarios.name: many_to_one
scenarios.description: One payment settling two invoices, and one invoice settled by two payments. Each is several pairs that share an entry, and the tree can be solved exactly.

scenarios.name: ambiguous_cycle
scenarios.description: Two 500.00 invoices and two 500.00 payments all cross-matched. Four pairs over four entries: the applied total per entry is exact, the pairwise allocation is not unique, and it is reported rather than invented.

scenarios.name: unsupported_history
scenarios.description: An invoice and a payment that e-conomic shows as fully applied, with no matched pair in the extraction. Closed state is visible; who paid what is not.

scenarios.name: inconsistent_match
scenarios.description: A pair whose entries do not conserve (300.00 applied to the invoice, 200.00 to the payment) and a REST remainder that disagrees with the ledger line. Both must block.

scenarios.name: cutover_boundary
scenarios.description: Cutover 2026-09-30. An invoice after the boundary is excluded; an earlier invoice paid by a post-boundary payment keeps only its snapshot residual because the API exposes no match date.

scenarios.name: manual_and_opening
scenarios.description: An opening balance, a journal-posted manual customer invoice (no booked-invoice resource, no PDF) and a reminder line. Only the first two are importable as open balances.

scenarios.name: control_total_disagreement
scenarios.description: Ledger lines reconcile document by document but the vendor's customer balance is 500.00 away, as seen once on the public demo company. Reported, never averaged away.
